candidates.attacker_control: The attacker fully controls the HTTP request target. HttpRequestParser.handlePath()/handleFullUrl() decode (and, with default settings, leave intact) '%2e%2e' and literal '..' segments and store them via exchange.setRequestPath()/setRelativePath() without canonicalization. The attacker can also choose the deployed context prefix and trailing file segment, e.g. GET /<context>/x/../WEB-INF/web.xml or GET /<context>/x/../../../../etc/passwd.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Global search shows CanonicalPathHandler is only defined (core/.../CanonicalPathHandler.java) and referenced in javadoc, never installed by DeploymentManagerImpl (checked deploy() flow, DeploymentManagerImpl.java:203-217); ServletContextImpl.getResource() does canonicalize (ServletContextImpl.java:311-317) but DefaultServlet does not use it, it calls the ResourceManager directly; FileResourceManager's canonical-name comparison does block some malformed paths (trailing '..', wrong-case final component) but not traversal with a real final file name; ClassPathResourceManager-style deployments may not resolve '../' through the classloader, so impact depends on a filesystem-backed manager. No test or runtime confirmation is available in the snapshot.
candidates.impact: Unauthenticated disclosure of files readable by the server process. Within a web application this exposes /WEB-INF/web.xml (data-source credentials, security constraints, internal endpoints) and, with additional '../' segments, files outside the deployment root such as /etc/passwd or application configuration. Only read access is demonstrated; no write/execution primitive follows from the source alone.
candidates.prerequisites: A servlet deployment whose resource manager is filesystem-backed (FileResourceManager / CachingResourceManager over a directory, the normal exploded-WAR layout); the request must reach the default servlet/static resource path; no front wrapper canonicalizes the path (DeploymentManagerImpl.deploy() only adds HttpContinueReadHandler and an optional URLDecodingHandler, and no CanonicalPathHandler is installed by the deployment itself). The traversal must keep a valid final path segment (FileResourceManager rejects paths ending in '.'/'..' because getName() mismatches), and the target extension must not be in DefaultServlet's disallowed set (only class/jar/war by default, so xml, properties, txt, etc. are permitted).
candidates.root_cause: Undertow decodes the request path but never canonicalizes it before servlet path matching and resource lookup. ServletInitialHandler.isForbiddenPath() (ServletInitialHandler.java:101-107, 164-167) and DefaultServlet.isAllowed() (DefaultServlet.java:318-348) check the raw path, so '/foo/../WEB-INF/web.xml' passes both; DefaultServlet.getPath() (DefaultServlet.java:293-316) then returns a path containing '..' and calls resourceManager.getResource(path) directly (DefaultServlet.java:134), bypassing the canonicalizing lookup in ServletContextImpl.getResource(). FileResourceManager.getResource() (FileResourceManager.java:80-103) builds new File(base, path), and its only sanity check compares file.getCanonicalFile().getName() with file.getName() - i.e. only the last path segment - so traversal passes whenever the final segment is a real file name (canonical 'web.xml' vs raw 'web.xml'), and the OS resolves the '..' at exists() time.
candidates.title: Non-canonicalized servlet path lets '../' escape the deployment root and disclose files (e.g. WEB-INF/web.xml)
candidates.trace: 1) HttpRequestParser decodes and stores the path without canonicalization (HttpRequestParser.java:338-399, 439-444); CanonicalPathUtils exists but is not invoked here. 2) The context PathHandler strips the context prefix and sets the remaining relative path verbatim (PathHandler.java:48-57). 3) ServletInitialHandler.handleRequest() checks isForbiddenPath() on the raw relative path, which matches only '/web-inf/'/'/meta-inf/' prefixes, so '/x/../WEB-INF/web.xml' passes (ServletInitialHandler.java:101-107, 164-167). 4) ServletPathMatchesData resolves the default servlet for the raw path; ServletPathMatch.getMatched() is the full raw path (ServletPathMatch.java:33-50). 5) DefaultServlet.getPath() returns that raw path and isAllowed() permits it (extension 'xml' not disallowed), then resourceManager.getResource(path) is called directly (DefaultServlet.java:128-134, 293-348). 6) FileResourceManager.getResource() resolves new File(base, 'x/../WEB-INF/web.xml'), exists() returns true, getCanonicalFile().getName() ('web.xml') equals getName() ('web.xml'), so a FileResource is returned and served (FileResourceManager.java:80-103).
candidates.unverified: Not runtime-verified and not built/tested. It was not confirmed from source which ResourceManager DeploymentManagerImpl installs by default for arbitrary deployments, nor whether common callers (e.g. WildFly) wrap the deployment with CanonicalPathHandler; both would affect real-world exploitability. Exploitability of ../ beyond the base directory depends on filesystem layout and depth of the deployment root.
candidates.weakness_type: Path traversal / arbitrary file read (CWE-22, CWE-20)

coverage_summary: Reviewed the assigned 595-file snapshot: core HTTP request parsing (HttpRequestParser, HttpTransferEncoding, PathHandler), servlet request/response and dispatch (ServletInitialHandler, ServletPathMatches/Data, DefaultServlet, HttpServletRequestImpl/HttpServletResponseImpl, RequestDispatcherImpl), static resource serving (FileResourceManager, DirectoryUtils, ResourceHandler, ResourceManager), security mechanisms (Basic/Digest/Form/SSO, SimpleNonceManager, SecurityContextImpl, SecurityPathMatches), handlers (ACL/IP ACL, proxy, form, encoding, cache, error pages), and util classes (URLUtils, CanonicalPathUtils, PathMatcher, Cookies, HeaderMap/Headers). This is not a full line-by-line read of every file; the snapshot is also pruned (many referenced classes such as io.undertow.conduits.*, HttpResponseConduit, Pipelined/ServerFixedLength conduits are absent), so cross-file reachability for some paths could not be fully traced.
limitations: Static, read-only review; no code execution, build, tests, or runtime confirmation.

The snapshot omits many classes referenced by retained files (e.g. io.undertow.conduits.*, HttpResponseConduit, ServerFixedLengthStreamSinkConduit, PipeliningBufferingStreamSinkConduit), limiting end-to-end traceability.
No tests, deployment descriptors, or external configuration are included, so the default ResourceManager per deployment type and any front-end canonicalization wrapper remain uncertain.
The traversal candidate depends on a filesystem-backed resource manager; classpath-backed deployments may not be affected.
Only the single strongest candidate is reported per the one-candidate cap; other leads are listed as rejected/unconfirmed.

rejected_leads.lead: HTTP response splitting / header injection through unvalidated header values (Headers/HeaderMap/HttpResponseConduit)
rejected_leads.reason: HttpResponseConduit and related conduit classes are absent from this snapshot, so the write path could not be verified; no concrete tainted header source was traced in the retained code.

rejected_leads.lead: Digest authentication nonce replay / nonce-count enforcement weaknesses (SimpleNonceManager, DigestAuthenticationMechanism)
rejected_leads.reason: The code is complex but has explicit first-use, overall and post-expiry windows; no clear bypass was demonstrated from source and the mechanism requires prior challenge/response interaction.

rejected_leads.lead: IPAddressAccessControlHandler IPv4/IPv6 wildcard and CIDR matching errors
rejected_leads.reason: Matching logic is only configurable at deployment time (no attacker-controlled rule input) and no bypass was proven; impact requires a misconfiguration.
Decoding and credential verification look conventional; no weakness (e.g. bypass or timing issue) could be substantiated from source.

rejected_leads.lead: AJP protocol request parsing (AjpRequestParser / server-side AJP exposure)
rejected_leads.reason: Could not establish an attacker-controlled file read/write path in this version from the retained sources; excluded as unconfirmed.
HttpTransferEncoding uses chunked-in-preference-to-Content-Length and takes the first Content-Length; no concrete parser differential could be confirmed without the missing conduit/parser classes.

summary: This is a source-only review of an Undertow 1.0.16.Final snapshot (595 files; core, servlet, websockets-jsr, examples). The strongest source-supported issue is an unauthenticated path-traversal / arbitrary file disclosure reachable through the servlet stack: request paths are decoded but never canonicalized before servlet matching and resource resolution, `ServletInitialHandler.isForbiddenPath` and `DefaultServlet.isAllowed` are evaluated against the raw path, and `FileResourceManager.getResource` only compares the final path-component name against its canonical form, so `..` segments survive and are resolved by the filesystem. No other issue reached the same evidence threshold; the analysis is static and not runtime-confirmed.
